pages.title: Blasts
New blast
pages._note: A multi-step wizard with a compliance gate, which no declarative type expresses. Advancing is conditional (canAdvance), the audience can be split into an A/B pair (abEnabled), and before a blast may be sent the page runs preflightCompliance + validateTemplate and blocks on awaitConsentDecision — the lawful-basis and unsubscribe-footer checks from the marketing-compliance spec. A declarative form submits; it cannot hold a send back pending a compliance verdict.

PerformanceDashboard.vue stays a custom page (pipelinq-dashboards-declarative kept-custom). It is a three-tab post-send analytics surface (Overview / A/B testing / Attribution), not a KPI dashboard: there are no headline metrics to lift into endpoint stat widgets, and the entire body is interactive tabbed content the declarative type:dashboard cannot express. Tab 2 computes a 2x2 chi-square p-value (analytic erfc survival fn) over click rates CLIENT-SIDE per A/B pair and gates the verdict on >=500 delivered + 24h elapsed; Tab 3 does an N+1 fan-out (one GET /api/blasts/:id/attribution per blast) and sums attributed deals/EUR; Tab 1 is a client-sortable table over blast totals with an id->name segment lookup. Missing primitives: (1) a tab-container body primitive (a dashboard cannot host a role=tablist switcher); (2) a client-side derived/statistical widget source (the chi-square significance verdict is not an endpoint scalar); (3) an N+1 per-row enrichment fetch (attribution is one request per listed blast, not a single aggregation endpoint).
pages.title: Blast performance
Blast monitor
pages._note: Declarative pages render a snapshot; this one is live. It owns a polling lifecycle (startPolling / stopPolling / clearInterval on unmount) and derives send progress from it — progressPercent, processed, audienceTotal, etaLabel and a buildTimeline series — plus an in-flight cancel action guarded by canCancel. There is no declarative primitive for a page that must keep refetching and be torn down cleanly.
